not really sure where this conclusion came from, but (at least to my understanding) it's not correct.  MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.

Thresholds I agree, are optional, and probably 50/50 for whether or not they're defined.

> MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.

This arguable but not true. ;)

1) I know for certain phosphor-virtual-sensor _only_ emits a {Min,Max}Value if one is explicitly enabled in the config, which is not required and many do not.

2) PLDM doesn't implement these in some cases.  https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/0b06dd891c42103a4555a0376e7a47b604f01ca9/platform-mc/numeric_sensor.cpp#L482

3) Not everyone uses IPMI so there is no certainty that anyone is testing even the IPMI side of it.

> > MinValue and MaxValue are required for IPMI to build SDRs, so they're arguably implemented by every sensor.
> 
> This arguable but not true. ;)

I said they were implemented, which we agree on.  Maybe it requires something defined in a config, but it does have an implementation.

But it still implements them.

Fair.  FWIW, I read the commit message first before I saw the code content.  Commit message seems pretty reasonable, and I'm not here to be a stickler for commit messages, so closing this out.

> so closing this out.

But it still implements them.

For some reason there are two different constructors in PLDM.  One of them doesn't implement (the one I linked to).  It just sets the value to NaN.
I think they're often set to NaN and not Inf?

This isn't really correct.  null in redfish means "supported but not yet populated".  Non existence for threshold on dbus has classically meant not supported.  we need to grok that distinction, and ideally in this commit message back it up with spec language.
Redfish service validator?
Overall I am good

Overall, there's more issues with the commit message more than the actual diff, which really shouldn't hold things up.

Lets just be consistent, which should simplify the code, and then this should be good to go.
7 year old TODO here 😊

Don't statically allocate maps at runtime.  They consume memory in inconsistent ways.

If this is staying, just declare as an array of string_view, and use std::find_if.

Also, if we end up keeping, please sort lists like this.  The order here is semi-random.
Is there any reason we limit this list?  This was limited to Value initially because that was where unavailable was, but in theory we could just make this not a per-value branch?
I'd much rather we keep this flow simple, and have the same behavior for each one.  If they're present but non finite, we populate with null.
